items.title: Phil Flanigan interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Diego, California, February 15, 1998
items.q: Loren Schoenberg is the source of this story, because he was working for him. He was sort of a secretary and business manager.

ctx.x: I’ve read it, but you can tell it.

Well it’s just basically Loren Schoenberg is the source of this story, because he was working for him. He was sort of a secretary and business manager. He would sit at the desk and answer the phone and run out to the drug store or whatever. And he asked Benny to copy some music and he needed some paper and this whole long story. Anyway Benny made sure that — there was three xerox copier machine outlet places there, with three different copiers in his apartment on 66th Street, because he’s made an American Express…
Oh, God. © Hamilton College Jazz Archive -13-

items.title: Loren Schoenberg interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 14, 2019
items.q: the band on that record was Dick Katz, Howard Alden, Phil Flanigan

ctx.x: players and — it was about fifty percent young and fifty percent older, of course much — the old guys were younger than I am now. And so the band started to cotton. And in the meantime Goodman asked me to come back because this woman I had mentioned before, Muriel Zuckerman, who had been his Girl Friday, she quit, and he said, “Can you come in and just, until I find someone, answer the phones or just help with something?” So I started doing that, and then eventually when he found out that I knew musicians and I…

Later on, as the band got professional and as I started to make a living in music, all those guys, I mean I paid. I paid for arrangements. I paid arrangers and I paid — but at this time there was nothing there. So John Hammond and a few other things and things started, and next thing you know we’re going to make a record. So we made a record for a guy named Jerry Valburn who issued a lot of radio broadcasts with like a big jazz collector who had his own little labels. And he had a label and he started recording…

he had a Mercedes. So on some weekends I would actually drive Benny up with Carol to their house, like the chauffeur, drive them up to Stamford, leave them, then I would drive his car back and park it in his garage. And I mean I had never driven a Mercedes Benz but that’s another story. Drive it back, park it in his garage, and somehow they would get back on Sunday.
